> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16e348642039be54d75eb96847af60f2919641e4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `41ef4246a23ba68334960dc1feacf8bf67cd4515` — the merge of head `8cad649c97cac01493b98ede4c87a20d396b5725` into base `16e348642039be54d75eb96847af60f2919641e4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 41ef4246a23ba68334960dc1feacf8bf67cd4515 && git checkout 41ef4246a23ba68334960dc1feacf8bf67cd4515
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 16e348642039be54d75eb96847af60f2919641e4 8cad649c97cac01493b98ede4c87a20d396b5725 && git checkout -B drift-repro 16e348642039be54d75eb96847af60f2919641e4 && git merge --no-ff 8cad649c97cac01493b98ede4c87a20d396b5725

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16e348642039be54d75eb96847af60f2919641e4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 16e348642039be54d75eb96847af60f2919641e4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `d7916e2f0217111f98e19072f12f5e95d97d4b15`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Reviewed: the net diff `origin/main...pr-33185` (9 files, +783/−27), card #32712 with every comment (ruling B′ 6842088322, evals 6842586067 / 6842606859, claim 6867767971 and amendments 6867825002 / 6867905360, os-dev-report 6868561765), the PR body, and the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff (`display-name.ts`, `engine-reference-name-visible.ts`, `security-plugin.ts`, `read-audit.ts`) was read for context only, not reviewed. Line numbers are at the head.

**Ruling B′, item by item**
- Two rows for the link's own user: holds. `targetRows` (upload-link-page.ts:187-205) builds the Record row (title, then label only, then not-yet-created) and the Goes-into row (field label, or Attachments). All text goes through `escapeHtml`. The rows go in the body only. The script literal (upload-link-page.ts:236-252) carries `expiresAt`, `now`, `expired`, `lang` and no name. The tab title stays `copy.pageTitle`.
- Read as that user, no system read: holds. `namesForLinkUser` (record-file-access.ts:1229-1281) resolves the user with `resolveUserContext`, the same call the upload uses (:1242, cf. :1397). It then calls `engine.findOne(..., { context: user })` (:1251), the same read `readRecordAs` does (:788-807), so object-level, field-level and RLS middleware apply as on the user's own read. The read runs only after `openLink` has passed (:1166-1179, called from `inspectUploadLink`), so a stranger, an expired link, a used link or an unknown token never reaches it.
- Degrade in steps: holds for text-typed titles. A missing or masked title gives the label only. A missing label drops the row. Any non-refusal failure gives today's page with one warn (:1244, :1255, :1279).
- **Never an id, API name or user: does NOT hold** for a display field that is not a text type. See MF1.
- A no-longer-readable record gets the same 404: holds. No row (:1257), a 403/404 throw (:1254) and a null user (:1246) all call `refuseUnusableLink()`. That lands in the route's existing catch (storage-routes.ts:1864-1871), which runs `sendUnusableUploadLinkPage`. Status, body and `pageHeaders` (upload-link-page.ts:55-67) are the stranger's, byte for byte except the nonce. Only the null-row leg is pinned (SF1). The extra read happens only for the link's own user, after the identity check, so a third party cannot observe any timing difference.
- Expiry in the reader's time zone and page language: holds. The time element is rewritten with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(T.lang, …)` (upload-link-page.ts:129-131), and the server's UTC text stays when no script runs. The server's clock is used as claimed: `skew = T.now − Date.now()` (:126), and `now` defaults to the server's `Date.now()` at render (:212). The error is permissive by network latency, never stricter than the server. The boundary (expired once `end` is at or before `now()`) matches the server's `deadline` check against `this.now()` (record-file-access.ts:1174). Send is disabled at load, on pick, on send and on a timer (:128-140). The post-upload state is wrong, see MF2.
- The server's one unusable-link refusal is unchanged, and the PUT door is byte-unchanged. The only route hunk is the GET (storage-routes.ts:1861-1866). The PUT's own inspect still passes no options (storage-routes.ts:2487). `consumeUploadLink`, `upload-link-wire.ts` and every refusal string in `upload-link-copy.ts` are untouched.
- Scope: service-storage only, with no spec change. Holds (file list).

**Break attempts, answered**
- Hidden values, masked titles and API names in the HTML, attributes, script JSON, data-* or comments. The record object is never serialized: only `record[titleField]` is read (:1269), it is gated by `getQueryableFields` (:1284-1290), and it goes out as dd text. No data-* attributes and no HTML comments are emitted. The only attribute added is `datetime` (the expiry, already printed). Labels pass only through `declared()`, never falling back to `state.object` or `state.field` (:1313-1336). One leak exists: MF1.
- Does a page GET write, spend or extend the link? It spends nothing and extends nothing (openLink only reads). One write the PR does not mention is N1, the read-audit row.
- Security service missing or throwing. With no 'security' service registered (storage-service-plugin.ts:426-432), the served row is the answer (:1286, :1295). That is sound, because the engine then applies no field-level security either. If the service has neither method, or answers non-arrays, the check fails closed (:1287-1290, :1296-1299). A throw anywhere in the name read falls back to names nothing (:1278-1280). A throw in `resolveUserContext` gives today's page, not a 404 (:1243-1245), as the claim amendment states.
- Readable but not queryable: label only, which fails closed. Queryable but not readable cannot happen by the contract (security-plugin.ts:3282-3307, the queryable set is the readable set minus masked fields), and the read strips unreadable columns anyway.
- A formula display field is evaluated in the user's own read, so it shows what the console shows that user. No system-elevated hop exists here, unlike the referenceNameVisible path. A lookup, user or select display field leaks: MF1.
- Pre-record link: object label plus field row. The field row asks `getReadableFields` as the user. Attachments link: Attachments row. Multi-file field: the rows do not depend on `files.min`/`max`. The tests pin an existing record's multi-file field, plus pre-record links of count 1 (single-file field) and count 3 (multi-file field).
- Localization. All 11 `CopyLocale` tables carry the 8 new members, which the interface makes non-optional, so tsc enforces completeness, and upload-link-copy.test.ts calls each one. Labels go through `translateObject` with the i18n service's fallback and default locale (:1323-1336), falling back to the declared label, never to an API name. An object with no declared label drops the Record row, which fails in the safe direction (unpinned, as the dev reported).

**Findings**
- **MF1 (must-fix): the title is not gated on a title-eligible field type, so the page can show an id or a user.** `resolveDisplayField` honours an explicit `nameField` "even if it is not currently title-eligible" (packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:225-238), and nothing refuses such a pointer. In-tree objects already point it at non-text fields: sys-session and sys-scim-subject point `nameField` at `user_id`, sys-record-share at `recipient_id`, sys-recycle-bin at `record_id`. When the display field is a lookup, master_detail or user field, its served value is the bare foreign id (ADR-0104 D1). For a select it is the machine token. `titleOf` (record-file-access.ts:694-698) rejects only objects, blanks and the record's own id, so the page prints `Expense "acc_…"` or a user id. That breaks B′'s "never shows an id, an API name, a user". The repo's own title-disclosure path gates exactly this case (packages/objectql/src/engine-reference-name-visible.ts:247-255: `isTitleEligible(def) || def.type === 'autonumber'`, plus `maskingRule == null`). Fix: apply the same gate to the field definition at :1268-1271, so a non-eligible type shows the object label only, and pin it with a lookup-`nameField` fixture.
- **MF2 (must-fix): the expiry timer overwrites the upload's answer.** The timer set at load (upload-link-page.ts:132) is never cleared, and `lapsed()` (:128) writes `status` whenever the moment passes, even after the PUT has answered (:151, :154). A user who uploads and leaves the page open until expiry (at most 10 minutes later) sees "Done. The file was attached…" replaced by "This link has expired. Ask for a new link.". The page then tells someone whose file landed to get a new link and upload again. On a multi-file field that adds a duplicate. On a pre-record link a second file waits. A send that is still in flight at the expiry briefly shows the expired line too. The "live" leg of the client-expiry test (record-file-access.integration.test.ts, the "once the printed expiry has passed" case) stops at `en.attached` and never fires its pending timer, so the pin misses this. Fix: once a send starts, stop `lapsed()` from writing (a settled flag, or `clearTimeout`), and fire the timer after the attached answer in the test.
- **SF1 (should-fix): two of the three 404 paths are unpinned.** A user who can no longer act in the org (`resolveUserContext` gives null, :1246) and a record read that throws 403/404 (:1254) have no test and no ablation. Only the null row after an ownership move is pinned. Both are ruling paths ("a user who left the org").
- **SF2 (should-fix): `security_findings: "withheld|none"` in os-dev-report 6868561765 is not an answer.** It is the template's alternation left unresolved. The report field needs one value, and given MF1 that value is not "none".
- **N1 (nit):** "Opening the page writes nothing" is true for sys_file, the link row and the record. But the name read is a primary-key-pinned detail read as the user, so on an object opted into read audit (packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/read-audit.ts:347-358) every page open enqueues a `read` ledger row. That is an honest record of a view, because the page shows the title. Scope the claim; the code is fine.
- **N2 (nit):** `translationBundleOf` (record-file-access.ts:706-713) rebuilds every locale's bundle on each page GET to translate two labels. This is acceptable at this traffic. Reading only `lang` and the fallback would be cheaper.
- **N3 (nit):** copy style is inconsistent. en lowercases "a new … not created yet" and "the "…" field" (per the ruling's wording), while es-ES, fr, pt-BR, ru and de capitalise ("Un registro nuevo…", "El campo…"). ko and pt-BR mix curly quotes (`recordTitled`) with straight quotes (`intoField`) (upload-link-copy.ts).
- **N4 (nit):** the PR body's "refuses nothing new" is loose. The GET now answers the unusable 404 where main served 200 for an owner who can no longer read the record or act in the org. B′ mandates this, and the PUT already refused both cases (record-file-access.ts:1397-1404, and `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` on the update), so no working path is removed and the widening arm stands. Only the wording is off.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-storage: patch` is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: the diff touches no `packages/spec` file and no authorable key. AGENTS.md maps a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, to patch. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds. The HTTP page shows more to its own user. The type surface widens only optionally: the `inspectUploadLink` options arg, `UploadLinkView.names`, `RecordFileAccessDeps.getI18n`, the two security read methods on `getSecurity`, and `sendUploadLinkPage`'s `now` default. None of these are new required members. The one new GET refusal (N4) removes no path that worked, since the PUT already refused it, so it is not the narrowing arm. The declaration lines match between the PR body and the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Surface: all 9 paths sit inside claim 6867767971 plus amendments 6867825002 (storage-service-plugin.ts: the getI18n binding only, :1469-1477) and 6867905360 (file-attachment-service.ts: pass-through only, :152, :167, :377-383). No breach. `upload-link-wire.ts` is untouched.
- Face: `reviewFace` finds no schema or governed path and the changeset declares no narrowing, so the declaration face applies at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no Scope line and no ④.
- Gates: at 2026-11-14T00:40Z the head's check-runs read 20 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure and 13 in_progress (Build Core, Test Core 1–8, three Type Check legs, Live E2E UI). The gate verdict is incomplete; this review does not lean on it.
- Dev flags. Out-of-scope 1: the stale comment at packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts:548 is confirmed comment-only. Its `not.toContain(EXPENSE_LINE)` and email assertions still hold, and Dogfood Regression Gate passed. It goes to a follow-up, not this PR. Out-of-scope 2: an object with no label drops the row. Confirmed safe, and a pin would be welcome but is not required. Security: see SF2 and MF1.
- open_questions: `UPLOAD_LINK_TTL_SECONDS` (record-file-access.ts, 10 minutes, untouched) is the card owner's call, not this review's, and the PR correctly leaves it alone. Eval 6842606859's case (two agent-minted links dead before the user arrived) warrants its own card. The client-side expired line now at least names the case without new disclosure.
- Premise: item (a) on main is reported as measured. That the eval saw a pre-#32891 build is labelled an inference in the PR body, and that holds as an inference.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-ddgmfc`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibzuZJBQY4wUQFJbkfx`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8cad649c97cac01493b98ede4c87a20d396b5725`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

This is a delta round on the record for `d7916e2f02` (FAIL: MF1, MF2, SF1, SF2). I read the delta `d7916e2f..8cad649c` (2 commits, 4 files, +168/−17; `d7916e2f` is an ancestor, so no other path moved), the net diff where it was needed, the new PR body and os-dev-report round 2 (6869128153). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed. Line numbers are at `8cad649c`.

**MF1 (title from a non-title field): closed.**
- record-file-access.ts:1277-1282 takes the title only when the display field's definition exists and is title-typed: `isTitleEligible(def)` or `type === 'autonumber'`, with `maskingRule == null`.
- This matches the first three legs of the engine's own gate (packages/objectql/src/engine-reference-name-visible.ts:247-255): the definition exists, it is title-eligible or the autonumber primary, and it declares no masking rule. The field-readability leg is covered here by `getQueryableFields`, which is stricter.
- The gate's fourth leg, a formula that reads through a reference, is correctly not carried over. That gate reads the name under elevation (its header, :50-60). This page reads as the caller, and a formula's hop is read as the caller through RLS and FLS (#24197, engine-master-detail-related.ts:560-572). A text formula title therefore serves exactly what the user's console title serves.
- Remaining paths to an id or a select value: none found.
  - An explicit `nameField` on a lookup, master_detail, user, select or any other ineligible type now shows the label only.
  - A `nameField` naming an undeclared field gives no definition, so no title.
  - With no explicit pointer, `deriveDisplayField` only ever picks title-eligible fields and skips injected platform text columns (display-name.ts:193-231). The new gate re-checks that pick anyway.
  - `isTitleEligible` admits a formula only with `returnType`/`valueType` text (display-name.ts:121-131).
  - What is left is author data: a text column or text formula whose content happens to be an id. That is the record's own title as the console shows it, not a page disclosure.
- Pinned: the `trip` fixture (lookup `nameField`, record-file-access.integration.test.ts:251-260, case at :1170-1188) asserts the served value is the bare foreign id. The page then shows the label only, in en and zh-CN, and no byte of the body or headers carries either id or the referenced title.

**MF2 (expiry timer over a send): closed.**
- The script's state is now `timer`, `busy` and `done` (upload-link-page.ts:129-141).
  - Send sets `busy` and runs `disarm()` (clearTimeout) before anything else (:148).
  - Success sets `done` (:160), and `lapsed()` then answers true without touching the line (:134).
  - A failure or lost connection goes through `settle()` (:137, :163-164). That clears `busy`, writes the answer, and re-arms only while the link has time left.
  - `lapsed()` while `busy` records the expiry but does not write the line (:134).
- Race check:
  - A pick after `done` returns early.
  - A cleared timer that fires anyway is inert after `done` and silent while `busy`.
  - A failure re-arms exactly one timer: the earlier one was cleared, and the button stays disabled after a failure, as on main, so no second send can stack timers.
  - An unparsable expiry arms nothing (`NaN` fails both the bound check and the time-left check).
- No race leaves the line wrong or Send enabled on a dead link. See R1 for one cosmetic leftover.
- Pinned at :1306-1351: a landed file stays "attached" after the timer fires and after a pick. A running send keeps "uploading" through the moment, and its answer then wins. A failed send re-arms the timer, and when the moment comes it flips to "expired" with Send disabled.

**SF1 (unpinned 404 legs): closed.**
- A user removed from `sys_member` gets the stranger's 404 byte for byte, and the page names the record again once they are a member (:1120-1137). That pins `resolveUserContext` answering null (record-file-access.ts:1253).
- A `findOne` that throws 403 or 404 gets the stranger's 404 byte for byte (:1139-1165, pinning :1261).
- The 500 arm is correct under B′. The ruling says "if nothing can be read, the page shows today's sentence". Claim amendment 6867825002, which the seat accepted, says "any other failure gives today's sentence". A 500 is an outage, not a refusal, so treating it as "can no longer read" would turn a transient fault into a dead-link answer. Degrading discloses nothing: no names are shown, and the PUT still judges the record itself. The test asserts status 200, no definition list, and that the title is absent.

**SF2 (report's security field): closed.** os-dev-report 6869128153 answers `security_findings: "none"`. That stands once MF1 is closed.

**N1 / N4: scoped as asked.** The PR body now scopes "writes nothing" to the sys_file, link and record rows, and names the read-audit row. It also states that the GET's new 404 is mandated by B′ and that the PUT already refused those cases. N2 and N3 are left as they were, which is acceptable for nits.

**New findings**
- **R1 (nit).** When a failed answer arrives after the moment has passed, `settle()` shows the server's refusal (the four-way unusable sentence) and does not arm. `expired` stays false, so the page does not add its own "expired" line. Send is already disabled, so nothing is sent into a dead link. Calling `lapsed()` in `settle()` when no time is left would give the clearer line.
- **R2 (nit).** The `maskingRule` leg of the title gate is unpinned, as the PR body discloses. With a security service present, masking is already pinned through `getQueryableFields`. The declared-rule leg only matters when no service is running, and then nothing masks the user's own read.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from round 1. `@objectstack/service-storage: patch` is right: no spec file and no authorable key are touched. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold. The delta adds no exported member and narrows nothing for a working caller. The changeset body now names the title-type gate and the send-owned status line, which is accurate.

### ③ Boundary flags
